Messages.Author: Doug
Messages.Body:
If the Nosferatu Bestial is in play and gets superior Animalism can he
use his special to employ a Raptor (or any other suitable retainer) at
superior? Someone in my play group argues that because it doesn't
specifically state that it can be employed at ANI that it only works
at inferior.

Nosferatu Bestial [Anarchs:R]
Cardtype: Action

Clan: Nosferatu

Cost: 1 pool

+1 stealth action. Unique.
Put this card into play. This card represents a unique Nosferatu
vampire with 2 capacity and basic Animalism. The Bestial cannot act
except to hunt, cannot cast votes and cannot have equipment. During
your untap phase, this Bestial may employ a retainer from your hand
that requires Animalism (he or she must meet the requirements of the
card). Pay the cost as normal. This is not an action and cannot be
blocked.

Thanks
Doug

it says it _has_ basic animalism. it doesn't say that the employing of
the retainer is at basic animalism, it just says _requires_ animalism,
with no mention of what level.
it does, however, mention that the Bestial must meet the requirments
of the card. So if Bestial has superior animalism, then it can employ
retainers that require superior animalism.

same goes for muricia's call at inferior animalism. you can still
employ the retainer you find in your library at superior animalism, if
you have it.

Messages.Author: Glen Robinson
Messages.Body:
I have a question:

Can a card that would force Bestial to do some other action (eg : Lunatic
Eruption: attack another minion, unless you must hunt), what happens? If
Bestial has blood (and thus doesn't HAVE to hunt), it MUST attack another
minion (which it can't).

I see a couple of possible solutions:

* The action cannot be preformed on Bestial
* The action fails
* Bestial is 'stuck' for the duration of the card effect
* And (unlikely), Bestial must do as told

LSJ?

Pahoehoe!

It'd be interesting to Spirit Marionette a Bestial just for novelty
value (you'd get to take whatever other action you want with one of

after blocking, but with spirit marionette's +1 stealth you'd be able
to slip someone through after you stole the bestial. a perfect plan
with no flaws whatsoever. and i am sure it will come up in every

Messages.Author: Andrew Daley
Messages.Body:
"Glen Robinson" <glen_r...@optusnet.com.au> wrote in message news:<3f03d125$0$728$afc3...@news.optusnet.com.au>...

> I have a question:
>
> Can a card that would force Bestial to do some other action (eg : Lunatic
> Eruption: attack another minion, unless you must hunt), what happens? If
> Bestial has blood (and thus doesn't HAVE to hunt), it MUST attack another
> minion (which it can't).
>
> I see a couple of possible solutions:
>
> * The action cannot be preformed on Bestial
> * The action fails
> * Bestial is 'stuck' for the duration of the card effect
> * And (unlikely), Bestial must do as told

I see this issue being like trying to get the Beast(!Nos) to have a
piece of equipment or a retainer. Restrictions on the vampire must be
obeyed. (Rules out the fourth option).

You are able play Lunatic Eruption on the Bestial (ruling out the
first and second options - there is nothing prohibiting the resolution
of the action). The only thing the Bestial can do is hunt, if needed
(at zero blood). This is due to the Bestial's restriction that stops
the directed attack action from occuring, thus cancelling the
mandatory action of lunatic eruption. Hence, the card text on the
lunatic eruption prevents the Bestial from performing any other action
it would normally be allowed to perform due to the limiations of the
Bestial and the Lunatic Eruption.

However, in that same minion phase, if another minion takes an
undirect action and removes the lunatic eruption, the Bestial is then
free to do an action as permitted by its inherent card text.

What do you reckon Gleno? :)

Andrew.
